entry.title: Seamless Mobile-to-Web Single Sign-On with the Joule Work mobile app
entry.content:
With version 3.0, Joule Work mobile app (formerly known as SAP Mobile Start) introduces a feature that many customers have been asking for: seamless Single Sign-On when opening web applications in the in-app browser. In this post I want to explain the problem this feature solves, how it works conceptually, and what administrators need to configure to enable it.

The Problem: Two Sessions, One App Experience

Joule Work mobile app (formerly known as SAP Mobile Start), when connected to SAP Build Work Zone, is the native mobile entry point for the Intelligent Enterprise. From a single app, users can access native features like widgets, push notifications, and smartwatch complications, but also launch web applications directly from the app – for example SAP Fiori apps from SAP S/4HANA, collaborative Workspaces in SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition, custom extensions build on the SAP Business Technology Platform, and more.

When a user taps on a tile that opens a web application, the Joule Work mobile app instantiates the in-app browser provided by the mobile operating system – iOS or Android. This is a technical context switch: the native application session, which is managed by SAP Mobile Services and backed by SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication, is logically separated from the browser sessions of web applications, for example SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition.

As a result, the in-app browser may not have a valid session for the target web application when launched. The user is redirected to the identity provider and prompted to log in again. This is particularly jarring because, from the user's perspective, they are just navigating within their app.

The Previous Recommendation – and Why It Was Not Ideal for all customers

Customers could avoid this by enabling the "Remember me" functionality of SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication. This feature creates a long-living session cookie in the browser, keeping users signed in across browser sessions for a configurable duration. A similar capability exists on many corporate identity providers (third-party IdPs) to which SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication may be configured delegating the actual authentication. Long-lived cookies on these providers effectively keep the user session alive in the in-app browser in the same manner.

However, this approach has a fundamental drawback: long-lived session cookies are not ideal and may not be wanted to be generically configured on the company's Identity Provider. Furthermore, "Remember me" only prolongs the time until a user is asked to sign-in again in the in-app browser – it is not fully getting rid of it.

Another alternative that some customers consider is password-less sign-in using client certificates. While this is a genuinely secure and, once set up, a convenient approach, it is not feasible for all customers and all users. Client certificates typically require an active Mobile Device Management (MDM) system to push certificates to managed devices – meaning unmanaged devices, common in bring your own device (BYOD) environments, are excluded. Beyond the deployment challenge, mobile operating systems restrict access to the system keychain for third-party apps, so not all in-app browser variants can reliably make use of client certificates. Other password-less options such as FIDO passkeys or biometric-based flows can require some form of manual user interaction during authentication, which breaks the seamless experience users expect when tapping a tile in the app.

The New Solution: Mobile-to-Web SSO

With version 3.0, Joule Work mobile app introduces a dedicated Mobile-to-Web Single Sign-On flow that bridges the native session and the in-app browser – securely, without requiring long-lived cookies. Here is how it works conceptually:

The mobile app already holds a valid session with SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication (in the context of SAP Build Work Zone, to which the app is connected to). The SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant generally serves as the trust anchor for both SAP Build Work Zone, the native app and other SAP and non-SAP solutions including web applications exposed to SAP Build Work Zone. This shared trust is what makes it possible to bridge the two worlds: because both the native app session and the target web applications are anchored in the same SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant, it can act as a secure intermediary, translating the native session into a web session in the in-app browser without requiring the user to authenticate again.

When the user opens a web application in the in-app browser, the app first exchanges its active native session for a short-lived, one-time use SSO token issued by SAP Cloud Identity Services. This token is valid for only a very short time and can only be used once by the mobile app for (re-)establishing a session in the in-app browser on the mobile device.

This is done by passing this one-time SSO token to SAP Cloud Identity Services within the browser context. The SAP Cloud Identity Services validates the token, maps it to the user's identity & native session, and establishes a regular web session – setting the standard browser session cookies. From there, the accessed target web application authenticates against SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication transparently via its standard SAML or OIDC flow reusing the established IAS session with no user interaction required.

The key properties of this approach:

  • Security-friendly: The SSO token is a one-time use token with a short validity. There are no long-lived session cookies involved on the identity provider side.
  • Admin-controlled: The feature can be controlled via a feature flag in SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit of the Joule Work mobile app. The administrator also defines exactly which web applications are trusted for this flow by configuring them in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication.
  • Broadly compatible: The feature works with all in-app browser variants offered by Joule Work mobile app on iOS and Android. It also works with all web applications – SAP solutions as well as custom or third-party apps – as long as they share a common SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication tenant with the environment the mobile app is onboarded to.

Key Prerequisite: SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication as the Common Trust Anchor

For the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow to work, SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication must be the identity provider for both the native mobile application and all web applications that should benefit from seamless SSO. The trust is established and maintained through SAP Cloud Identity Services, making it the single common denominator across all participants.

It is important to clarify that SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication does not need to be your end users' primary authentication system. In many enterprise landscapes, SAP Cloud Identity Services acts as an identity proxy, delegating the actual authentication to a corporate identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID or other identity providers. This is fully supported. The only requirement is that SAP Cloud Identity Services is the first common trust anchor in the chain – meaning all participating web applications are configured to trust it directly, even if it in turn proxies to a corporate IdP.

One configuration detail to be aware of in proxy setups: the "Forward All SSO Requests to Corporate IdP" setting in SAP Cloud Identity Services must not be enabled for the applications involved in the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow. When this setting is active, SAP Cloud Identity Services bypasses its own session handling and always redirects to the corporate IdP – which would cause the Mobile-to-Web SSO token to be ignored, and users would end up with a login prompt again. Beyond Mobile-to-Web SSO, enabling this setting can also cause issues in iFrame-based in-place app integration scenarios, as corporate identity providers frequently block iFraming to protect against clickjacking and similar attack vectors. For more information on this setting, see Forward All SSO Requests to Corporate IdP (SAP Help).

The trust for the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow is configured explicitly in SAP Cloud Identity Services. The administrator defines which web application entries in SAP Cloud Identity Services are allowed to participate in this flow – only applications that have been explicitly added to the trust configuration can benefit from it. In addition, SAP Cloud Identity Services validates the URL of the target web application against the allowed redirect URIs configured for the trusted application. This means a web application can only receive a seamless SSO session if its URL matches one of the permitted redirect URI patterns. Both aspects – the application trust list and the redirect URI validation – ensure that the administrator retains full control over which applications can be reached via this mechanism.

Please note: Customers with SAP Build Work Zone subscriptions created before March 2025 may not yet be using SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication directly. For these environments, it is necessary to explicitly switch the authentication mechanism. Subscriptions created after that date are automatically set up with SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication. Please refer to the SAP Help documentation for the migration steps: Switching to SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication.

Pro tip: As with other features that depend on shared sessions and cookies – such as the iFrame-based in-place integration of web applications – it is important that all components share a common super domain. We strongly recommend operating SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication and your SAP cloud solutions under the SAP Common Super Domain cloud.sap, while other domains work as well as long as they are aligned across the stack to prevent cross-domain restrictions. If you are not yet familiar with this topic, our earlier blog post explains the background and the configuration steps in detail: Demystifying the Common Super Domain for SAP Mobile Start.

Which Web Applications Are Covered Automatically?

When Joule Work mobile app is connected to SAP Build Work Zone, both share the same Application entry in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication. This means that SAP Build Work Zone itself is automatically within the trust scope – no additional configuration is needed for it.

This automatic coverage includes for example:

  • SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition Workspaces – collaborative workspace content embedded in the Work Zone experience
  • Custom extensions hosted on SAP BTP – applications built for example with the SAP Cloud Application Programming Model, deployed to the SAP BTP and served using the Approuter of SAP Build Work Zone. (For details on building such extensions, see Building Pro-Code Extensions for SAP Mobile Start)
  • SAP Fiori apps from SAP S/4HANA On-Premise or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition running through an SAP Cloud Connector using a Principal Propagation Destination – these are tunneled through the BTP subaccount and are therefore covered by the same Application entry

The key distinction is that automatic coverage applies to applications that are part of – or tunneled through – the SAP BTP subaccount and its corresponding SAP Cloud Identity Services Application. Applications that run on their own infrastructure and have their own independent trust relationship with SAP Cloud Identity Services are not automatically covered, regardless of whether they are launched in embedded ("in-place") mode or opened directly ("ex-place"). A prominent example is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: even when it is iFramed within the SAP Build Work Zone shell, it has its own Application entry in SAP Cloud Identity Services and must be explicitly added to the Native-Web Trust group.

For all such web applications – SAP solutions with their own IAS Application entry, third-party apps, or any app not part of the Work Zone BTP subaccount – administrators add them to the trust configuration in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication as described in the setup steps below.

Administrator Setup

Step 1: Verify That IAS-Based Authentication Is Active

Before enabling the feature, confirm that SAP Build Work Zone is using SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication as its identity provider. If this is not yet the case, follow the migration steps referenced in the prerequisite section above.

Step 2: Enable the Feature Flag in SAP Mobile Services

In the SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit, navigate to the Client Settings. In the Feature Flags section, locate the entry named "MobiletoWebSingleSign-On" and activate it.

Screenshot showing the highlighted feature flag in the activated state in the Mobile Services Admin Cockpit.

For reference, the corresponding documentation can be found here: Single Sign-On for Web Apps – SAP Help

Step 3: Add Trusted Web Applications in SAP Cloud Identity Services

For web applications that are not automatically covered through the SAP Build Work Zone application (see the previous section), you can add them to the trust configuration:

  1. Sign in to the administration console for SAP Cloud Identity Services.
  2. Go to Applications & Resources → Applications.
  3. Select the application entry that corresponds to your SAP Build Work Zone instance.
  4. Go to the Trust tab, then navigate to Application APIs → Dependencies → Native-Web Trust.
  5. Click Add and select the application with which you want to establish trust.
  6. Save your selection.

Screenshot of SAP Cloud Identity Services to maintain Native-Web Trust Settings

Users opening applications from this trust list in the in-app browser will now benefit from the seamless Mobile-to-Web SSO flow.

Step 4: Verify the Redirect URIs of Trusted Applications

As described in the prerequisite section, SAP Cloud Identity Services validates the URL of the target web application against the allowed redirect URIs of the trusted application entry. For SAP-delivered solutions – such as SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition – the redirect URIs are typically pre-configured correctly by SAP and no further action is needed.

However, for custom-built applications or third-party web apps that rely on the general SAP Business Technology Platform application entry in SAP Cloud Identity Services, you should verify that the application's URL is covered by the configured redirect URI patterns. If the URL does not match any permitted pattern, the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow will not complete successfully for that application.

You can review and adjust the redirect URIs in the SAP Cloud Identity Services administration console under the application's configuration. For the rules and wildcard syntax supported for redirect URIs, refer to the SAP Help documentation: Redirect URIs and Post Logout Redirect URI Rules (SAP Help).

Summary

With the Mobile-to-Web SSO feature, Joule Work mobile app version 3.0 closes the session gap between the native app context and the in-app browser – cleanly, securely, and with full administrator control.

Key takeaways:

  • The feature eliminates the need for long-lived "Remember me" cookies on the identity provider, which are a security concern and not universally available.
  • It is based on short-lived, one-time use SSO tokens issued and validated by SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication, which acts as the common trust anchor.
  • The feature is optional and in control by the customer: an administrator (de-/) activates it via a feature flag in SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit of Joule Work mobile app and controls which web applications participate via the Native-Web Trust configuration in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication.
  • SAP Build Work Zone web UIs and tunneled embedded business apps are automatically covered. Additional apps can be added with a few clicks.
  • The feature is compatible with all in-app browser variants in Joule Work mobile app and all trusted web applications, regardless of whether they are SAP solutions or custom apps.

If you need further assistance configuring and making use of this new feature in the Joule Work mobile app, feel free to contact our product management team using jouleworkmobile@sap.com, which will be able to suggest the next steps for your scenario.

  • Joule Work mobile app – Single Sign-On for Web Apps (SAP Help)
  • Switching to SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication (SAP Help)

entry.title: SAP Service and Asset Manager: New Release Strategy Incoming
entry.content:
If you're working with SAP Service and Asset Manager (SSAM) — whether as a customer, partner, or someone evaluating the solution — there is news worth paying attention to. We are changing the way we release SSAM, and I believe this change will make a real, tangible difference to everyone who uses it.

Let me walk you through what's changing and why it matters.

 

 

From Two Major Releases a Year to One — With a Purpose

Until now, SAP Service and Asset Manager shipped on a cadence of two major releases per year. We are moving to a new model:

 

1 Major release + 3 Minor releases per year

This is not a slowdown. It is a deliberate shift in how we think about delivering value. Here is what the new model means in practice:

- Minor releases carry fewer new features — they focus on fixes, refinements, and incremental improvements

- No MDK version update in minor releases (security patches excepted) — the underlying Mobile Development Kit stays stable between major releases

- Mobile backend updates in major and 2nd minor release – Providing two crisp client-only upgrades

 For customers and partners, this means a much more predictable upgrade experience. Minor releases are safe and lightweight. Major releases are the moments where new capabilities and platform upgrades arrive.

 

The Release Roadmap

Here is how the new cadence looks across the next release cycles:

 

 

 

 

 

MDK Stabilization: One Upgrade Per Year

The Mobile Development Kit (MDK) is the technical foundation that SSAM is built on. Under the new strategy, MDK version upgrades are aligned exclusively with major releases — meaning one upgrade per year at most.

For anyone who has managed SSAM deployments, this matters. It means your environment stays on a known, stable MDK version between major cycles. No unexpected changes mid-year. No cascading compatibility issues you didn't plan for.

 

What You Should Do Now

If you are on an earlier SSAM version or planning a new deployment, the roadmap above gives you a clear view of what is coming and when — use it to align your project timeline with the right release.

I am excited about where SAP Service and Asset Manager is going. A more frequent release rhythm to bring exciting improvements, and major milestones on the horizon. This is a product being built to last.

entry.title: Warehouse Clerk Persona in SAP Service and Asset Manager
entry.content:
Introducing the SAP Service and Asset Manager Warehouse Clerk Persona for EWM

 

End-to-End Warehouse Execution in a Single Mobile App

The Warehouse Clerk persona supports the core warehouse execution processes required by organizations running SAP EWM. It covers the complete warehouse lifecycle, from inbound processing and storage operations to outbound fulfillment and inventory management. 

The Warehouse Clerk persona empowers warehouse operators to execute critical warehouse activities directly from a mobile phone or tablet, whether they are connected online or working offline. By complementing traditional RF-based user experiences with a modern, user-friendly mobile application, organizations can improve productivity, simplify user adoption, and provide warehouse workers with real-time access to operational information.
 

Inbound Processing

Receiving goods efficiently is essential to maintaining inventory accuracy and warehouse throughput. The Warehouse Clerk persona enables warehouse workers to:

  • Process inbound deliveries
  • Perform goods receipt activities
  • Create warehouse tasks
  • Execute putaway operations through warehouse task confirmation
  • Create and maintain Handling Units (HUs)
  • Support single, multi-item, mixed, and auto-packed handling unit scenarios
  • Perform inbound delivery adjustments and updates directly on mobile devices

These capabilities help streamline receiving operations while reducing dependency on desktop systems. 

 

 

 

 

Warehouse Task and Order Management

Warehouse execution revolves around warehouse tasks and warehouse orders. The Warehouse Clerk persona provides a comprehensive mobile experience for managing both.

Users can:

  • Download warehouse orders assigned through Resource Management
  • Search for warehouse orders and tasks on demand
  • Confirm warehouse tasks
  • Process multiple warehouse tasks efficiently
  • Work with warehouse orders, tasks, and associated inventory objects from a single interface

This flexibility allows organizations to support both resource-managed and manually driven warehouse processes. 

 

       

 

Handling Unit Management

Handling Units are central to warehouse execution within SAP EWM. The Warehouse Clerk persona offers extensive support for HU-related activities, including:

  • Creating Handling Units
  • Maintaining and updating existing Handling Units
  • Packing and repacking inventory
  • Supporting serialized and batch-managed products
  • Performing warehouse task confirmations involving HUs

By integrating these functions into the mobile experience, workers can complete operational tasks directly where the work happens. 

 

Outbound Processing

Outbound execution is another major focus area of the Warehouse Clerk persona.

Supported outbound activities include:

  • Processing outbound deliveries
  • Creating warehouse tasks for picking operations
  • Confirming picking tasks
  • Handling packaging activities
  • Managing outbound-related Handling Units
  • Supporting goods issue processes

These capabilities help ensure smooth order fulfillment and warehouse execution from picking through shipment preparation. 

 

 

 

 

Physical Inventory Management

The Warehouse Clerk persona enables mobile inventory execution through:

  • Physical inventory counting
  • Inventory document processing
  • Download and management of inventory work items
  • Inventory synchronization with backend SAP systems

Workers can perform stock verification activities directly within the warehouse while reducing paperwork and manual data entry. 

 

Resource Management Integration

Capabilities include:

  • Resource search
  • Resource assignment visibility
  • Claim Resource functionality
  • Release Resource functionality
  • Download of warehouse orders and tasks assigned to the active resource

This ensures that work is distributed efficiently and that operators always have visibility into their assigned workload. 

 

Built for the Modern Warehouse Worker

Beyond process coverage, the Warehouse Clerk persona includes a rich set of mobile-first capabilities designed to improve usability and productivity.

 

Advanced Search and Scanning

Users can quickly locate operational objects by:

  • Barcode scanning
  • Camera-based scanning
  • Direct search
  • Ad hoc lookups for warehouse orders, tasks, products, bins, and inventory objects

Enhanced scanning serves as one of the key pillars of the Warehouse Clerk user experience.

 

Offline Execution

Warehouse operations do not stop when connectivity is interrupted.

The Warehouse Clerk persona supports offline execution, enabling users to continue working and synchronize data once a connection becomes available again. This is particularly valuable for large warehouses where network coverage may be inconsistent.

 

Exception Handling

Real-world warehouse processes rarely follow a perfect path.

To support operational flexibility, the Warehouse Clerk persona includes exception handling capabilities such as:

  • Quantity differences
  • Split operations
  • Destination changes
  • Warehouse execution exceptions

This allows users to resolve process deviations without leaving the mobile workflow.

 

Personalization and Mobile UX

The mobile experience includes usability enhancements that improve efficiency for daily warehouse work:

  • Mobile-optimized workflows
  • In-app personalization options
  • Process switching and configuration
  • Tablet and smartphone support
  • Simplified navigation focused on warehouse execution tasks

The result is a modern user experience designed specifically for mobile warehouse operators.

 

 

 

Deployment Flexibility and EWM Alignment

The solution supports:

  • Decentralized EWM deployments

This allows organizations to adopt mobile warehouse execution while leveraging their existing SAP EWM investments.

 

The Future of Mobile Warehouse Operations

The Warehouse Clerk persona represents a significant step forward in bringing SAP EWM warehouse execution processes to a modern mobile platform. By combining inbound processing, warehouse task management, handling unit operations, outbound fulfillment, physical inventory, resource management, advanced scanning, offline capability, and exception handling into a single mobile application, organizations can empower warehouse workers with the tools they need to execute efficiently from anywhere in the warehouse.

As the solution continues to evolve, the Warehouse Clerk persona is establishing itself as a comprehensive mobile execution platform for SAP EWM customers seeking greater productivity, improved user experience, and streamlined warehouse operations.

entry.title: Reimagining Filters on Mobile: A Natural Language Approach in SAP Fiori Elements
entry.content:
Target Audience: Developers, UX Designers, Business Analysts, SAP Architects
Reading Time: 5 minutes

Let's look at how we use our phones at work today. We check reports on the go, approve requests between meetings, and look up customer details on the way to the next appointment. Our phones have quietly taken over as the primary work device and enterprise apps are still trying to keep pace.

But there's one interaction that still slows us down: filtering data.

Picture a familiar scenario: You're heading for a meeting and want to quickly check for overdue invoices above 10,000 EUR. You open the app, ready to get the number. A few minutes later, you close it and tell yourself you'll check from your desk later.

If that sounds familiar, you're not alone.

In this article, we'll explore:

  • Why mobile filtering has felt like a workaround for so long
  • What the industry has tried, and where those approaches fall short
  • What users have really been asking for
  • How a new approach in SAP Fiori elements is finally delivering the experience that users deserve

Let's take a closer look.

Why Mobile Filtering Falls Short

Filtering on a mobile phone has always felt more like a workaround than a workflow. And the reason is simple: filter bars were designed for desktops, not for a device meant to fit in the palm of your hand. When we take the same filter bar and place it on a 6-inch screen, even the best-designed applications end up delivering a subpar experience.

It's not that users can't filter on mobile phones. They can. It's just that the experience makes it far harder than it needs to be.

 

Where the Experience Breaks Down

Users filtering on mobile phones run into the same usability issues, regardless of how well the application is designed. Here's what typically gets in the way:

  • Labels too small to read comfortably
  • Tightly packed dropdowns that lead to incorrect selections
  • Date pickers demanding exact input
  • An Apply button that isn't visible without scrolling

The result is almost the same. The user gives up the task and waits until they're back at their desk. 

For a mobile-first workforce, this isn't a small inconvenience. It's a real barrier to getting work done.

What We've Tried Before

The mobile filtering problem isn’t new. Over the years, the industry has tried several ways to solve it. Each approach has moved the needle a little, but none has fully solved the problem.

Here are the most common approaches and where they fall short:

  • Responsive design: Stacks filter fields vertically to fit small screens. The layout improves, but the underlying complexity remains. Users still work through the same dense form, only with more scrolling.
  • Simplified filter sheets: Removes advanced filtering options and retains only the basics. The UI feels cleaner, but users lose the depth and precision they need for real business scenarios.
  • Quick filters: Offers predefined options for common use cases such as "My Open Items" or "Due This Week". They work well for predefined scenarios, but the moment users demand something ad-hoc, the approach breaks down.

What Users Actually Want

A clear pattern emerges when we watch how users interact with filters on their mobile phones. They don’t want to configure the filter bar or tap through dropdowns. What they want is simple:

"Just let me describe what I'm looking for."

This single expectation captures the change users have been waiting for. And it is exactly the experience the AI-powered natural language filter delivers.

From Filter Bars to Conversations

That's exactly what the new AI-powered natural language filter in SAP Fiori elements is built to deliver. Instead of selecting values in complex filter forms, users can simply type or speak what they're looking for. A simple phrase like "overdue invoices above 10,000 EUR" is all the AI needs.

Behind the scenes, the AI understands the intent, aligns it with the application context, and translates it into a precise OData filter. This is the same kind of filter the application would've applied if the user had gone through the traditional filter bar. The results appear on screen, filtered exactly as the user described.

The best part is that this capability works on top of your existing SAP Fiori elements applications.

  1. Enroll through your SAP account executive
  2. Contact the SAP EAC team
  3. Align your IT organization on adoption
  4. Access the experience from your mobile using the Joule Work app

What's Next in This Series

In the next article, we'll go under the hood and explore:

  • The three-stage architecture

  • Privacy and security foundations

entry.title: Reimagining Filters on Mobile: The Engine Behind It
entry.content:
Target Audience: Developers, UX Designers, Business Analysts, SAP Architects
Reading Time: 6 minutes

Filtering data on a mobile phone has always felt harder than it should. In the first article of this series, we explored why traditional filter bars fall short on small screens and introduced the AI-powered natural language filter in SAP Fiori elements — a capability that lets users simply type or speak what they're looking for. In this article, we go under the hood and walk through the engine that makes it work.

How It Works: A Three-Stage Architecture

At its core, the AI-powered natural language filter follows a simple three-stage architecture. Each stage plays a distinct role: understanding the user's intent, aligning that intent with the application context, and producing a precise, executable filter.

 

Let's walk through each stage in detail.

Stage 1: Understanding the Query

The first stage focuses on interpreting the user's request. Whether the input is typed or spoken, the AI analyzes it and breaks it down into three tasks: intent classification, entity recognition, and context enrichment.

Intent Classification

The AI determines the nature of the request. A single query may express one of several intents:

 

Intent Example
Filtering"Show me overdue orders"
Sorting"Newest first"
Search"ACME Corp"

Identifying intent ensures that the query is understood and translated correctly.

Entity Recognition

Once the intent is clear, the AI identifies the meaningful components from the query, such as field names, values, and operators.

 

TypeExamples 
Field NamesStatus, Amount, Date, Customer
ValuesOverdue, 10000, Last Week, ACME
OperatorsAbove, Below, Between, Equals

This structured breakdown allows the AI to build precise filter conditions, rather than relying on keyword matching.

Context Enrichment

Finally, the AI uses the parsed query to align it with the business context of the application. This includes:

  • Mapping business terminology to technical field names
  • Resolving relative dates, such as last week and next quarter
  • Handling synonyms and alternate business terminology

 

Query PhraseInterpretation
"Overdue"Maps to status filter
"Past due"Interprets as status = Overdue
"Last week"Calculates to a specific date range

Stage 2: Aligning Intent with Metadata

Understanding the user's query is only the first step. To translate that intent into a valid OData filter, the AI translation engine needs to know what the application supports. This is where OData annotations come in. Rather than making assumptions, the AI uses metadata to understand the following:

  • Available filter fields
  • Data types
  • Allowed values
  • Semantic meanings

Here's a sample metadata snippet:

{
  "technicalName": "OverallStatus",
  "label": "Status",
  "type": "Edm.String",
  "values": ["Open", "InProcess", "Completed", "Overdue"]
}

With this metadata, the AI translation engine can now do the following:

  • Map "status" to the technical field OverallStatus
  • Recognize "Overdue" as a valid value
  • Identify that Amount is a currency field
  • Associate the query "Created" with the CreationDate property

Stage 3: Generating the OData Filter

Once the query is understood and mapped with the metadata, the AI translation engine generates the precise OData expressions that the back-end can execute directly.

Here are a few examples of simple queries:

 

User QueryGenerated OData Filter
"Overdue orders "OverallStatus eq 'Overdue'
"Amount above 10000 "GrossAmount gt 10000
"Created last week "CreationDate within calculated date range
"Customer ACME Corp "substringof('ACME', CustomerName)
"Urgent items from purchasing org 1010 "Priority and PurchasingOrganization filters

The AI can also combine multiple conditions into a single, well-formed filter expression.

Here's how a complex query gets broken down and translated:

Phrase Interpretation Generated OData Filter
OverdueStatus filterOverallStatus eq 'Overdue'
Invoices above 50,000Amount comparisonGrossAmount gt 50000
EURCurrency filterCurrency eq 'EUR'
From last monthDate range (resolved)CreationDate ge '2026-05-01' and CreationDate le '2026-05-31'

What the Filters Can Understand

The AI-powered natural language filter is designed to understand how users express their data. It interprets five categories of queries:

  • Status and Enum Filters: Enumerated values, such as status, priority, and category, are among the most common filter criteria. The AI recognizes valid business values by referring to value-list annotations in the service metadata. Typical queries include "open orders ", "approved requests ", and "critical priority ".
  • Numeric Comparisons: The numeric operators expressed in natural language, including greater-than, less-than, and range comparisons. Examples include "Amount above 10000 ", "Quantity less than 50 ", and "Between 1000 and 5000 ".
    To interpret numeric values for currencies and units correctly, use the following annotations:
    • measures.ISOCurrency
    • measures.Unit
    These annotations correctly distinguish between values and units.
  • Date and Time Filters: Users mostly think of relative terms such as "last week " or "this quarter ", rather than exact dates. Such expressions are resolved into concrete date ranges. Common examples include "last week " and "this month ", as well as specific expressions, such as "after June 1st " and "Q1 2026 ".
    For example, if today is June 24, the phrase "last week " translates to the range June 17 – June 23.
  • Text Search: Text fields, such as customer names, supplier names, and product names, support exact and fuzzy matching, allowing users to search even when they remember only a part of the value. Queries can include "Customer ACME ", "Supplier contains Steel ", and "PO 4500012345 ".
  • Combined Filters: In a real-world scenario, users often combine multiple criteria in one sentence, and the AI-powered natural language filter identifies all conditions and appends them with the correct logical operators. Common queries include "open orders from customer ACME above 10000 " or "critical items created this week not assigned to me ".

Voice Input Support

Typing on a mobile phone isn't always practical for users who are on the move or wearing gloves. To address such scenarios, our AI-powered natural language filter also supports speech-to-text input, allowing users to simply speak their query instead of typing it.

For example, a user might simply say: "Show me overdue purchase orders from purchasing organization 1010."

Behind the scenes, the request flows through the following four steps:

  1. The spoken query is transcribed into text.
  2. The transcribed text is interpreted just like any typed input.
  3. The intent is translated into a precise OData filter expression.
  4. The filter is applied automatically, and results appear instantly.

Voice input unlocks productivity in the following situations where traditional input methods fall short:

  • Warehouse workers operating equipment or wearing gloves
  • Field sales representatives moving between customer visits
  • Shop-floor managers navigating production areas
  • Service technicians performing on-site inspections

Privacy and Data Security

Privacy and data security are foundational to any enterprise AI capability. The AI-powered natural language filter aligns with the enterprise-grade security principles designed by SAP, ensuring that intelligence is delivered without compromising trust or compliance.

Key Security Benefits

  • Business data is never sent to the AI model. Only the query text and service metadata are processed.
  • Filters are executed directly on the SAP S/4HANA back end, keeping data within your trusted environment.
  • Authorization checks remain fully in effect.
  • AI services run on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP).
  • No third-party AI providers are involved.

  • Enroll through your SAP account executive

  • Access the experience from your mobile using the Joule Work app

Joining the EAC Program delivers real advantages:

  • Early access to upcoming AI capabilities

  • Influence over future roadmap decisions
  • An opportunity to prepare apps before General Availability (GA)

What's Next in This Series

In the next article, we'll explore the following:

  • Mobile performance optimization
  • Offline capabilities

entry.title: SAP Service and Asset Manager 2511.2 Now Available - What's New?
entry.content:
Before we look at the new capabilities in 2511.2, it's worth noting that SAP Service and Asset Manager has transitioned from a biannual release cycle to a new quarterly cadence consisting of one major release and three minor releases per year. This approach enables more frequent delivery of enhancements while maintaining a predictable upgrade experience. To learn more about the new release strategy and what it means for customers, read SAP Service and Asset Manager: New Release Strategy Incoming .

 
Now, let's take a closer look at what's new in SAP Service and Asset Manager 2511.2.

Technicians and operational teams rely on SAP Service and Asset Manager to complete work efficiently, access the right information, and keep business processes moving in the field. With the 2511.2 release, we are introducing a broad set of enhancements designed to improve usability, expand process coverage, and make everyday work more intelligent and efficient.

This release includes new Joule capabilities, enhanced AI-assisted job completion, customer-created in-app guidance with WalkMe SDK, improvements to Phase Model support, map capabilities, configurable order dates, and a redesigned experience for handling synchronization errors. We are also expanding support for warehouse and field logistics processes with Outbound Delivery and Remote Kitting capabilities, while continuing to improve application performance through enhancements such as smarter delta synchronization.

Together, these updates help technicians and other operational users work with greater efficiency, better visibility, and more flexibility across maintenance, warehouse, and logistics scenarios.

Joule Enablement in SAP Service and Asset Manager

With Joule Mobile Client integration, technicians can access relevant information directly within SAP Service and Asset Manager. They can ask Joule for equipment details and maintenance history or use it to locate supporting documents, manuals, and additional work instructions.

Technicians can also ask Joule to summarize a work order, including essential details such as what needs to be done, where and when the work will take place, how it should be completed, and which parts may be required. To use Joule capabilities in SAP Service and Asset Manager, customers must complete the required Joule setup on SAP Business Technology Platform. Details can be found here: Joule Integration Configuration.

                                

 

                                       

 

 

Enhanced AI-Assisted Job Execution Completion

SAP Service and Asset Manager previously introduced AI-assisted job execution completion to help technicians record job outcomes more efficiently. With the 2511.2 release, this capability is enhanced to support notification activity codes as part of the completion process.

Instead of manually entering detailed completion information, technicians can describe the work they completed using speech input, including work duration, parts used, expenses, conditions or issues identified, and follow-up notification information. The app converts the speech to text and uses AI to interpret the input and generate the relevant job completion and notification details.

For example, a maintenance technician could describe completing an operation, the time spent, an additional O-ring that was used, travel and expenses, and details about a leaking pump. The technician could also provide the applicable damage, cause, and activity codes and request an update to an existing notification item—all through a single spoken description.

This creates a more natural and streamlined completion experience, helping reduce manual data entry while improving data-capture efficiency and supporting more complete and consistent maintenance records.

                         

 

WalkMe SDK Support for Customer-Created In-App Tutorials

Training and onboarding are essential for technicians using SAP Service and Asset Manager. However, because implementations are often configured around each customer’s specific business processes, standard training materials may not always address every organization’s needs.

With the 2511.2 release, SAP Service and Asset Manager introduces WalkMe SDK support, allowing customers to create and integrate their own tutorial content directly into the app experience. This enables organizations to provide contextual guidance based on their configured processes and help technicians learn directly within the application.

 

Note: WalkMe integration is supported on iOS with the 2511.2 patch release, Android support is planned for the upcoming 2511.3 release.

 

Enhanced Phase Model Support

SAP Service and Asset Manager also expands Phase Model support to provide greater flexibility for different maintenance scenarios. The enhancement supports "minor work with screening" and "emergency work with screening" processes, allowing screening of minor and emergency maintenance requests. Also, technicians can provide Failure effect when creating notifications, providing more details on asset failure and its impacts.

These enhancements help customers better support different types of maintenance work and capture the information required throughout the maintenance process.

 

 Map Enhancements

Maps provide technicians with important location and business information while working in the field. With this release, SAP Service and Asset Manager enhances the map experience with support for grouping business layers, helping users organize and manage map information more effectively.

The release also supports returning feature layer properties from the map, providing greater flexibility for customers that use map-based information as part of their mobile workflows.

 Configurable Order Start and End Dates

Different organizations may use different date fields to plan and manage maintenance work. Previously, SAP Service and Asset Manager provided a single date property for this purpose.

With the release, two configurable properties are introduced for the start date and end date of an order. Customers can map these properties to the SAP date fields that best fit their business requirements, providing greater flexibility in how order dates are presented to technicians.

 Improved User Experience for Synchronization Errors

Synchronization errors can occur when technicians are working with mobile data, but understanding the cause of an error and the transactions affected by it is important for resolving the issue efficiently.

With the 2511.2 release, SAP Service and Asset Manager introduces an improved experience for synchronization errors. Instead of relying primarily on a text-based error message, technicians can more easily review errors, access additional error details, and understand related transactions. This provides users with greater visibility into synchronization issues and makes it easier to understand what went wrong and which transactions may be affected.

 Smarter Synchronization and Performance Improvements

Performance remains an important focus for SAP Service and Asset Manager, particularly for technicians who regularly synchronize data while working in the field.

With the 2511.2 release, Smart Sync Protocol improves mobile delta synchronization by pre-calculating which data has actually changed before the technician starts a sync. During synchronization, the app can refresh only changed objects while skipping unchanged data, reducing unnecessary processing and improving overall performance. This can reduce delta-sync duration by more than 50%, helping technicians get updated data faster without changing their existing workflow.

Outbound Delivery Support for Warehouse Clerks

The 2511.2 release also expands SAP Service and Asset Manager capabilities for the warehouse clerk persona with support for the Outbound Delivery process. Warehouse clerks can search, fetch, and download outbound delivery orders, including directly from the home screen. The process also supports working with outbound deliveries, creating missing picking warehouse tasks, confirming picking activities, and completing goods issue.

By bringing these activities into the mobile experience, warehouse clerks can perform more of their outbound delivery workflow directly within SAP Service and Asset Manager.

Remote Kitting for Field Logistics

For Field Logistics scenarios, the 2511.2 release introduces support for the Remote Kitting process. Users can fetch and download kits, review kit items, and perform key actions such as staging, issuing, and dropping materials. The process also supports undo actions, editing kit items, and removing downloaded kits from the device.

This extends the mobile Field Logistics experience and provides users with the capabilities needed to manage kit-related activities while working away from the primary warehouse location.

The 2511.2 release of SAP Service and Asset Manager brings together enhancements across intelligent assistance, maintenance execution, usability, logistics, and application performance. These capabilities help organizations provide their technicians and operational users with a more intelligent, efficient, and connected mobile experience—so they can spend less time navigating systems and more time getting work done.

entry.title: Joule Work on the Go and Mobile Design System Enhancements: What's New in SAP's Mobile Experience
entry.content:
In the first half of this year, SAP Fiori for Android and SAP Fiori for iOS as well as Joule mobile client have undergone a series of intelligent improvements aimed at elevating user experience and boosting productivity. These enhancements have introduced greater flexibility, consistency, and functionality across both platforms, ensuring that users can navigate their applications with ease and efficiency.

On top of that, the Joule Work app, formerly known as SAP Mobile Start, has been introduced at SAP Sapphire. With this app, complex tasks can be accomplished while on the go. Users simply need to define their goals and let AI take action.

 

Joule Work Mobile App

Joule Work is a central, intelligent workspace where AI takes charge of the busy work, enabling users to focus on driving outcomes. It transforms the work environment with a proactive, outcome-driven experience, where users articulate goals and AI coordinates actions across systems to accomplish them efficiently. Processes speed up considerably with proactive assistance, using the comprehensive business context of Joule Agents and Joule Assistants to highlight relevant data and suggest actions. This setup streamlines complexity, allowing users to focus on decision-making and outcome generation, while routine tasks are delegated to supervised agents. In addition to the web app, Joule Work offers a desktop app for faster access to local files and applications, as well as a mobile app for managing complex workflows on the go.

Conversations

Conversations act as dynamic interfaces for seamless interaction with Joule, making engagement intuitive and natural. Users can easily express their needs by typing, speaking, or attaching files, eliminating the need for traditional navigation methods. Joule enriches this process by offering context-based prompts, conducting platform-wide searches, and providing detailed answers with real-time data and interactive elements. By facilitating dialogue, conversations enable users to express their intentions and explore desired outcomes, drawing together insights and results from SAP and third-party systems. Moreover, conversations serve as entry points to spaces, supporting more complex workflows. This streamlined approach enhances user engagement and simplifies the pursuit of information and task completion.

Spaces

Spaces are dynamic, AI-generated workspaces tailored to match a user's intent, offering a seamless user experience. These adaptable environments allow users to engage in conversations and customize features without navigating through apps or dashboards, ensuring that individual needs are met efficiently. Within a space, tasks can be completed using natural language or structured inputs, fostering intuitive and effective interactions. Spaces are created in real time, pulling together the necessary data, tools, and context to achieve specific goals. They display only essential information through actionable summary cards, tables, metrics, or alerts, enabling users to focus on their tasks without distractions. These persistent spaces ensure users can easily return to continue their work from where they left off, facilitating both simple and complex problem-solving with ease.

Download for Android | Download for iOS

 

Joule mobile client 

The Joule mobile client, which facilitates the integration of Joule into Joule Work, provides exciting new features designed to enhance user interaction and streamline communication. Dictation allows users to harness the power of their device's built-in voice recognition, enabling hands-free messaging and smoother, more accessible conversation workflows with Joule. This innovation is perfect for busy professionals who need to multitask, as it allows them to communicate effortlessly without sacrificing productivity. The newly integrated typeahead feature intelligently offers contextual suggestions as users type. This predictive element cuts down on keystrokes and expedites prompt completion, resulting in more efficient interactions. Alongside these input features, Joule has also expanded its functionality with response actions, enabling users to easily copy or regenerate responses directly within the conversation. This means users can quickly reuse Joule's outputs or request new answers without retyping prompts, offering a seamless, user-friendly experience. Additionally, the transparency and explainability feature has been improved to provide users with clearer insights into Joule's AI-generated replies, ensuring they understand the response origins and details. Sources are now displayed separately from response insights, giving users straightforward access to the information that influences their conversations. Together, these updates demonstrate Joule’s commitment to enhancing user productivity and communication efficiency through innovative solutions while ensuring clarity and confidence in AI interactions.

 

What’s New in SAP Fiori for Android 26.1 and 26.4

Extended Card Header

The extended card header has been updated for greater flexibility, enabling you to place various components, such as tags, status indicators, or custom elements, together in a single row. This allows for more compact, streamlined, and versatile card layouts.

For more information, check out Card Header in the SAP Fiori for Android design guidelines.

Extended card header

Multi-User Onboarding

The user list now reflects SAP Fiori for iOS standards and displays users onboarded to a specific device, sorted from the earliest to the most recent.

For more information, check out Multi-User Onboarding.

Switching or adding a user

Step Progress Indicator

The nodes in the step progress indicator, which is designed to track and display a user's status within a user flow, now offer the same customization options as SAP BTP SDK for iOS. You can modify the size, layout, and icon in an icon node and specify different states for the icon node. When there are just a few steps, the width of each step expands to fill the screen, creating a more balanced layout.

Refer to Step Progress Indicator to find out more about this component.

Step progress indicator

List Picker Form Cell

A read-only state has been added to the list picker form cell, which allows for the selection of one or more options among values within a defined category. In this state, the selected value(s) are shown, and the chevron is removed. The cell height adjusts to ensure that all selected values are displayed without any truncation.

Learn more about the List Picker Form Cell.

List picker form cell

Switch Form Cell

The switch form cell, which allows users to turn on/off individual settings, now includes a read-only state. In this state, the toggle switch control is replaced with a text label that indicates the pre-set value. While the default label is “On/Off,” you can customize it to provide more contextual messages, such as "Included/Not Included."

See Switches for more details.

Switch form cell

 

What’s New in iOS 26.1 and 26.4

AI User Feedback

The AI user feedback feature lets users share their experiences with AI. The inline AI feedback entry point has been updated to function as a standalone, reusable component.

See AI User Feedback for more information.

AI inline user feedback

Step Progress Indicator

The step progress indicator, which monitors and shows a user's position within a user flow, has been enhanced. The width of each step node is now adaptable with a set minimum value, allowing the indicator to expand and fill the screen width when there are fewer steps visible.

Explore the Step Progress Indicator.

Step progress indicator nodes

List Picker Form Cell

The list picker now features a read-only state where selected values appear inline, the chevron is removed, and the cell becomes non-interactive. There is no word limit on displayed values. However, lengthy or multi-selected values might cause the cell height to stretch. To address this, we recommend either avoiding the read-only state or implementing a custom summary view.

Learn more about the List Picker Form Cell.

List picker form cells

Switch Form Cell

The switch form cell now includes a read-only state where a text label, defaulting to "On/Off," is shown instead of the visual switch. This label is fully customizable to offer more contextual messaging, such as "Included/Not Included." The form cell height and padding are consistent with the active state, ensuring a seamless layout experience.

Read more about the Switch Form Cell.

Switch form cell

 

UI Kits for Figma

With the updated SAP Fiori for Android and iOS UI Kits, it’s now easier than ever to use the latest components and patterns in your mobile design. By using the UI Kits, you can quickly create a consistent user experience that enables app implementations at scale.
